title: Seed Quantity Per Acre Calculator
description: Work out total seed needed from a per-acre rate with the Seed Quantity Per Acre Calculator — pounds, bags and seed counts for the whole field. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, wheat at 120 lb per acre over 40 acres needs 4,800 lb of seed — exactly 96 fifty-pound bags, a number the supplier's quote should match to the bag.
quick_answer: The Seed Quantity Per Acre Calculator multiplies a seeding rate by the field's acreage to give the total seed to buy — in pounds, bags or raw seed counts depending on the crop. Enter rate and acres and read the order quantity, before the planter is hitched.

body.t: Running out mid-field costs a day and a delivery fee. The calculator's total, plus a sensible margin, is the order — field size from the
Suppliers quote per bag, per unit, per pound. Total quantity in one unit makes the quotes comparable — arithmetic as negotiation armour.
Corn and soybeans are planted by population: 32,000 corn seeds per acre over 80 acres is 2,560,000 seeds — 32 bags of 80,000. The calculator speaks both languages.
Last year's partial bags subtract from this year's total. The calculator gives the gross; your store-room count gives the net.
140,000 seeds per acre × 25 acres = 3,500,000 seeds = 25 units of 140,000. Seed units exist so this multiplication lands on whole numbers.
Headlands, overlaps and a spilled bag argue for 5–10% over the bare total. The calculator gives the bare total honestly; the margin is your judgment, added openly.

faq: Yes — divide the target population by the germination fraction (a 90% germ tag needs ~11% more seed). The calculator totals the rate you enter; enter the adjusted rate.
Professional buyers compute PLS from purity × germination on the seed tag. This page's totals are the field arithmetic around that figure.
Acreage is acreage however the field is shaped — measure the drawn area and multiply. Shape changes drilling patterns, not totals.
Total the blend's rate, then split by the blend's percentages per component — the calculator handles the total; the ratio is the blend's label.
Most seed keeps a season if kept cool and dry, with a germination retest before relying on it. The order total can assume the retest, not the hope.
Bags are a different size here.
Enter the total weight the calculator gives and divide by your local bag size — the pounds are universal, bags are regional.
